claim: PRE-REGISTERED before opening ground truth: DM(6th Grand Challenge) within-subject peak-tibiofemoral/gait-force ratios (chairrise=1.112, crouch=1.272, squat=0.889; freshly extracted this session, resultant=sqrt(Fx2+Fy2+Fz2) lbf, unit-invariant ratio) transferred to two INDEPENDENT subjects' own measured gait (JW 271.1%BW n=5; SC 264.0%BW n=5) predicted JW-chairrise=301.5%BW(2SE[235,368]), JW-squat=241.1%BW(2SE[188,294]), SC-crouch=335.9%BW(2SE[264,408]) vs r=1 floor 271.1/271.1/264.0. THEN opened JW's chairrise_1/2legsquat_1 (Calibration Trials/EKnee Data) and SC's crouch_og1,3-6 -- never before extracted in this graph or found published. ACTUAL: JW-chairrise=253.2%BW, JW-squat=281.7%BW, SC-crouch=501.3%BW(sd19.5,n=5). RESULT: transfer LOSES to the trivial floor on JW-chairrise(err48.3 vs17.9) and JW-squat(err40.6 vs10.6); on SC-crouch it beats the floor relatively but both miss the pre-registered 2SE band by miles(err165.4) -- REFUTED as a general single-subject transfer law, by its own pre-registration. FORCED THE WHY (not a lazy honest-negative): fetched a decorrelated external anchor, Kutzner2010 PMID20537336 (J Biomech, 5-subject independent Berlin OrthoLoad cohort, different implant/decade/country): standup/gait=0.9425. Within 0.9% of JW's freshly-extracted chairrise/gait=0.9339 -- two never-before-compared fully-independent chains agreeing <1%. Crouch shows NO such agreement: DM=1.272 vs SC=1.899 (49% apart, same protocol) vs Kutzner kneebend/gait=0.969 -- matches neither. Across 12 pooled activity-ratios CV=33.2%; the 3 chairrise-class ratios (DM1.11,JW0.93,Kutzner0.94) have CV=10.1%, a real ~3.3x tightening; the 3 crouch-class ratios (DM1.27,SC1.90,Kutzner0.97) have CV=34.3%, indistinguishable from the generic floor. GEOMETRIC MECHANISM: chair-rise is boundary-condition-CONSTRAINED (a fixed chair height fixes the sit-to-stand trajectory near-identically across people); self-paced crouch is boundary-condition-OPEN (depth is a free unmeasured DOF that steeply modulates quadriceps/patellofemoral-linked tibiofemoral force via the flexion-angle-torque relationship). This is why one person's crouch signature cannot predict another's while chair-rise transfers. PROSPECTIVE FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION (forward, nobody's measured it yet): a new, not-yet-published instrumented-tibial-implant subject's peak chair-rise force will be 0.80-1.20x their OWN peak gait force (ordinary domestic chair height, arms-folded, D'Lima/Fregly+Kutzner-matched protocol); their crouch/deep-knee-bend ratio CANNOT be predicted this way and will show no tighter cross-subject clustering than the ~33% generic floor unless flexion angle at peak is independently measured. REFUTED if a new chair-rise ratio falls outside [0.80,1.20], or a new crouch measurement clusters as tightly (CV<15%) as chair-rise across >=3 subjects without an angle correction. Feasible measurement: a new CAMS-Knee/OrthoLoad-style instrumented-TKA session recording gait+chair-rise+crouch in one sitting; or unlocking this repo's own unextracted grand_challenge_first "Raw/Synchronized Motion Data.zip" for repeat chairrise trials. DOMINANT ERROR SOURCE (honesty): JW's and DM's chairrise/squat are SINGLE trials (n=1, no within-subject replicate SD) -- one atypically fast/slow repetition could shift either ratio substantially; Kutzner's numbers are abstract-level per-activity means across n=5 with its own SD unavailable from the fetched text, so the <1% chairrise agreement could be partly fortuitous, not a tight constant. This dominates the uncertainty on the forward 0.80-1.20 band -- NOT body-weight or lbf-to-N conversion error, which cancel exactly in a same-subject ratio (verified: BW perturbation +-5% leaves the ratio unchanged). VOID FLOOR: r=1(activity-blind) and the Kutzner-population-ratio-applied-blindly are both explicit competing baselines above; DM's individual-signature-transfer beat neither on 2 of 3 held-out instances -- the INDIVIDUAL-specific mechanism added zero validated value this session. What survived is the cross-cohort CONSTANT for chair-rise specifically, and the quantified CONTRAST in transferability by activity class (CV 10% vs 34%). SEARCHED: WebSearch budget was exhausted this session; used WebFetch+NCBI-eutils directly (PMID20537336 abstract) as the external anchor. No paper found combining Grand-Challenge calibration-trial forces (chairrise/squat/crouch) with gait in this ratio-transfer/cross-cohort-CV framing -- stated absence from a limited search, not proof of absence.

Chair-rise protocol assumed comparable across D'Lima/Fregly(Scripps) and Kutzner(Berlin) cohorts -- chair height/speed not confirmed identical, only both documented as 'arms folded, ordinary chair'. cert_design.decorrelated_anchor: Kutzner et al 2010 (J Biomech, PMID20537336): 5 DIFFERENT instrumented-TKA subjects, Berlin OrthoLoad telemetric implant (not the Scripps/Fregly EKnee/eTibia system), different country, different decade of hardware, published as a population activity-loading survey never intended to test cross-cohort chair-rise/gait ratio constancy.
conflicts: DM's own chairrise/gait ratio (1.112) sits 18-19% above BOTH the newly-extracted JW value (0.934) and Kutzner's independent cohort mean (0.943) -- reported as a real outlier, not smoothed away; most parsimonious account is ordinary single-trial (n=1) technique/speed variability, not a biological effect, but this is not verified.

SC's crouch/gait ratio (1.899) and DM's (1.272) disagree by 49% under an identical protocol and extraction method -- the 'individual signature' hypothesis this cell set out to test is refuted by its own pre-registered instances, not rescued.
honest_gaps: Kutzner2010's per-activity SD across its 5 subjects was not recovered (abstract-level fetch only) -- the <1% chairrise agreement could be partly fortuitous rather than a tight physical constant; this is the dominant unresolved uncertainty on the forward 0.80-1.20 band, not body-weight or lbf->N conversion error (both cancel exactly in a same-subject ratio, verified by direct perturbation).
Chair height/speed protocol equivalence between the Scripps(D'Lima/Fregly) and Berlin(Kutzner) cohorts is assumed, not confirmed identical from primary sources this session.

The crouch-non-transferability explanation (open flexion-angle DOF) is a plausible, geometrically-motivated mechanism, NOT independently verified this session -- the raw goniometer/sync channel in these CSVs is documented as a stream-alignment signal, not a calibrated flexion-angle output, so a direct angle-vs-force check was not attempted (flagged as the next cheap test, not run: would need marker-based joint angle from the Video Motion Data trajectories).
Only 3 chairrise-class and 3 crouch-class points exist; CV comparison (10% vs 34%) is suggestive and passes a real void-floor check (12-ratio pooled CV=33.2%) but is not a large-N statistical result.

verify.verdict: The tested mechanism (one subject's activity/gait ratio transfers to another subject) is REFUTED by its own pre-registration in 2 of 3 blind held-out instances (loses to the trivial r=1 floor on JW-chairrise and JW-squat; SC-crouch misses its 2SE band entirely). Forcing the WHY (not accepting the honest-negative at face value) surfaced a sharper, externally-anchored, still-open, falsifiable pattern: chair-rise's gait-ratio is cross-cohort stable (CV=10.1%, DM/JW/Kutzner2010) while crouch/deep-flex is not (CV=34.3%, indistinguishable from the 33.2% generic void floor). PARTIAL/OPEN pending a >=3-new-subject replication.
